clue.text: Model or tarted-up woman making brunch for one?

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A catwalk model, or a woman all dolled up, is making a late breakfast for one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun beside 'woman', but it is the anagram signal working on OR TARTED-UP WOMAN. The question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunch blends breakfast and lunch into one coined term, a classic example of a blended word.

clue.text: One whose work can be draining?

definitions.text: One whose work can be draining?

parts.words: One whose work can be draining?
parts.note: draining sounds like exhausting work, but this tradesperson literally deals with drains

explanation.walkthrough: 'Draining' tempts the reading of a tiring job; the literal sense of clearing drains and pipes points to the tradesperson.
explanation.definitionFit: This tradesperson fits and unblocks pipes, sinks and drains, so the work is literally about drainage.

clue.text: Mammal consumed food, tucking into game

indicators.note: the eating phrase signals one piece going inside the letters for the game

parts.note: RL is short for rugby league
consumed food means ate

explanation.surface: An animal ate its meal while tucking into some game it had caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' is the container signal. Rugby league, abbreviated, is the game; the mammal is the honey badger.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel, or honey badger, is a fierce African and Asian carnivore, a kind of mammal.

clue.text: Meteorologist initially guessing about humidity

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the following word is used
about here means the letters are moved around, rearranged

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster is making a guess about how humid it will be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning' but is the anagram signal; 'initially' gives only the opening letter of Meteorologist.
explanation.definitionFit: Mugginess is close, damp warmth in the air, which is the same thing as humidity.

clue.text: Write music, say, and outlast men oddly ignored

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are dropped, keeping only the even ones from these words

explanation.surface: Compose a tune and live longer than the men who strangely took no notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly ignored' drops the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of AND OUTLAST MEN, which leaves the even letters to spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate is to set down in written symbols, and writing a score is one example of that.

clue.text: Poor children leaving school at last after English improved

indicators.note: after means the rest comes after the abbreviation for English
poor means in bad shape, so these letters are put into a different order
leaving means a letter departs from the word children
at last means the final letter of the word school

explanation.surface: Poor children quitting school at the end of their schooling make their English better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' and 'leaving' drop school's final letter from the fodder, leaving CHIDREN; 'Poor' rearranges it, and 'after' places it behind the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich something is to raise its quality or value, so enriched means made better.

clue.text: Posh medic beginning to use revolting language

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: U means upper-class or posh
DR is short for doctor, a medic

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the word use

explanation.surface: An upper-class doctor starts to use disgusting language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like 'disgusting' but turns U + DR + U the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, also widely spoken in India.

clue.text: Upset husband interrupting public spat

indicators.note: interrupting means one letter breaks into the run of other letters

parts.note: overt means open or public
a spat is a quarrel, a row

explanation.surface: A husband breaking into a public quarrel is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interrupting' puts the husband's letter at the join between the two synonyms. 'Upset' is the verb, to knock over.
explanation.definitionFit: To overthrow is to topple or knock over, which is one sense of upset as a verb.

clue.text: Island's papers turned up to see wreck

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Elba is the Italian island where Napoleon was exiled, plus the S of the possessive
ID means identification papers

explanation.surface: The island's newspapers turned up to report on a shipwreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads ELBAS + ID upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To disable a machine is to put it out of action, much as wrecking it does.

clue.text: Angry at university reluctant to spend money

parts.note: up means at university, as in 'up at Oxford'
tight means stingy, reluctant to spend money

explanation.surface: Someone at university is cross and refuses to part with any cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Being UP means being in residence at a university, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight means tense and irritable, so it covers being annoyed or angry.

clue.text: Visible embarrassment as second transmitter goes west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading from right to left

parts.note: a sender is something that transmits

explanation.surface: Something embarrassing shows as a second radio transmitter breaks down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes west' sounds like 'breaks down' but reads S + SENDER right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A blush shows embarrassment, and the colour it puts on the cheeks is a redness.

clue.text: Projectile writer describes fully opening

indicators.note: describes means draws a line around, so the pen's letters go round the others

parts.note: Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, a writer
all means fully, completely
an opening is the first, written 1ST, with the figure 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A writer gives an account of a missile launch going fully ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describes' means drawing round, so the pen's letters enclose the rest. 'Opening' is first, written 1ST, with the digit 1 read as a letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballistic is the adjective for projectiles in flight, as in a ballistic missile.

clue.text: Crack constabulary is inspiring

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the word holds the answer within it

explanation.surface: The elite police force is a real inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like an adjective for an elite force, but it is the noun meaning an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a crack at something means having a try, the same as having a stab at it.

clue.text: Vulgar Republican adopts daughter, one manipulated by sailor?

indicators.note: adopts means taking someone in, so one letter is brought inside

parts.note: rude means vulgar

explanation.surface: A crude Republican takes in a daughter, then gets pushed around by a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adopts' puts D inside RUDE + R. The question mark warns that the sailor works the steering gear, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat's rudder is steered by whoever is at the helm, typically a sailor.

clue.text: Car about to be acquired by fellow Caribbean islander

indicators.note: being acquired means being taken in, so those letters go inside

parts.note: a don is a university fellow
the Mini is a classic British car
CA is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A car is about to be bought by another man from the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be acquired by' is the container signal; 'about' is circa, not a time phrase. The Mini is a small British car, and a don a university fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Dominica, or of the Dominican Republic, is an islander from the Caribbean.

clue.text: Tree regularly spreads in garden close to fence

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken from these words
close to means the last letter of the word fence

explanation.surface: A tree keeps spreading out in a garden right up to the fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the even letters of SPREADS IN GARDEN. 'Tree' is the family tree, not a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree is a recorded line of ancestry, which is what a family tree sets out.

clue.text: Supposedly offspring of necessity is porky?

definitions.meaning: the proverb says necessity is the mother of ..., making it necessity's child
porky, from rhyming slang porky pie for lie, means a made-up story

explanation.walkthrough: 'Porky' is British rhyming slang: porky pie = lie.
explanation.definitionFit: An invention can be a new device or a fabricated story, so it fits both the proverb and a fib.

clue.text: Investigation concerning school that's capturing attention

parts.note: re means concerning, about

indicators.note: capturing means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: giving an ear means giving attention

explanation.surface: An inquiry into a school is holding everyone's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's capturing' is the container signal: the school's abbreviation holds the attention word.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is systematic study to find facts out, which is an investigation.

clue.text: Person gambling gets team playing having lost one time, right?

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters move about and land in a new order
having lost one means a single copy of the letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A gambler gets his team playing, having lost once; is that right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having lost one' drops one of the two Ts from GETS TEAM; 'playing' rearranges GESTEAM to GAMESTE, and R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamester is an old word for a habitual gambler, someone who plays games of chance.

clue.text: Look towards student feeding extremely large creature

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily towards something

indicators.note: feeding means putting something in, so one letter goes inside the others
extremely means only the two outer letters of the word large

parts.note: L is for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: Watch a student feeding a huge animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes just the ends of large; 'feeding' puts the learner's L between them. L is for learner, from British learner-driver plates.
explanation.definitionFit: The gazelle is a slender, swift antelope of Africa and Asia, an example of a creature.

clue.text: Professed a love to embrace Victor and get married

indicators.note: to embrace means to hug, so these letters wrap round another one

parts.note: love is a score of nil in tennis, the letter O
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to wed is to get married

explanation.surface: A lover swore love, hugging Victor before they got married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To embrace' puts V between A and O, then WED follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Avowed means openly declared or acknowledged, which is what professed means.

clue.text: House in decay, gutted and filthy

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: nasty means filthy, foul

explanation.surface: A house fallen into decay, its insides torn out and dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' leaves DY from decay. 'House' is a royal family line, as in the House of Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal house is a ruling family line, and a dynasty is exactly such a line of rulers.

clue.text: Current energy requirement essentially must stop

indicators.note: to stop is to plug a gap, so this letter fills a space inside the other word

parts.note: steam means energy or vigour, as in 'run out of steam'

indicators.note: essentially means the central letter of the word requirement

explanation.surface: An energy requirement at this point must come to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' takes R, the middle of requirement; 'must stop' plugs it into STEAM. 'Current' is the noun, a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a steady flow of water, which is what a current in a river is.

clue.text: Region united behind leader of Zulus

indicators.note: behind means the piece for united comes after the first letter
leader of means the first letter of the word Zulus

parts.note: united as one means together, so one stands for united

explanation.surface: A territory has united behind the leader of the Zulu people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' puts ONE after Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone is an area or district marked out, which is a region.

clue.text: Add-on for individual office telephone

definitions.meaning: an addition, such as an added room to a house
a single phone line off a central office switchboard

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a building's added wing and a desk phone reached via the switchboard.

clue.text: Wife's sister perhaps through with teaching, some said

parts.note: in can mean through, during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: some said means the word sounds like another, at least in some accents

parts.note: lore means teaching, traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: Perhaps a wife's sister has finished with her teaching job, so some say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some said' admits LORE only sounds like LAW in accents that drop the R. 'Through with' looks like 'finished with', but through gives IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's sister is a sister-in-law, one example of a relative by marriage.

clue.text: Appearances of disheartened Poet Laureate

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart, the two central letters, is removed

parts.note: Ted Hughes was the UK's Poet Laureate from 1984 to 1998

explanation.surface: A Poet Laureate made a few public appearances, looking downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' looks like 'gloomy' but drops GH, the central pair, from HUGHES.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue is a colour or a look, so hues are outward shows or appearances.

clue.text: Large doubt mostly that Bill puts on hairspray

indicators.note: puts on means the piece for bill is placed before the next part

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a query is a doubt or question

explanation.surface: There's a big doubt about the bill that's been run up on hairspray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the doubt word's last letter; 'puts on' places the bill's abbreviation in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer is a sprayed fixing liquid, and hair lacquer is an old name for hairspray.

clue.text: Food items, some sacred, I blessed

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A priest blesses some holy food.
explanation.definitionFit: Edibles are things fit to be eaten, so the word is a plural noun for food items.

clue.text: Writer from Germany seen with criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer from Germany is seen in the company of a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun for the writer's companion, but it rearranges GERMANY SEEN WITH.
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist wrote The Old Man and the Sea and won the Nobel Prize for Literature.
